text: MSG-P7-009 answers one sentence naming the field and the case reference, with no rule value and no case attribute, and MSG-P7-012 answers one warning naming the chain position of the entry that does not verify. Until the catalogue is written, section 14 carries the placeholder rather than an invented sentence, and no criterion asserts the words.
why: Both message IDs are required by the criteria of this story and by the target criteria of the service, and no source writes either sentence; a story that invents a sentence would put an unapproved user-facing text into the build.

text: The case-creation read is the ledger read of API-P7-006 with one added query parameter finalCall and it answers a page of entries with entryId, caseRef, decisionCode, finalCall, ruleId, ruleVersion, inputsRef, decidedAt, actorUserId, prevHash, entryHash, chainSeq and chainVerified; no case-creation entry answers 200 with an empty page rather than 404.
why: The TSD read has no final-call filter and no projection, and the legacy key read the case through case endpoints that belong to another service in the target, so the filter and the field list have to be fixed as a default before the controller and the fake are built.

text: The case reference on decision_log_entry is an indexed business key of the text type with no foreign key and no relationship row to rwb_case, and the ALS business date travels inside inputs_ref; no case attribute column is added to rwb_decision and no case row is read to fill the entry.
why: The target forbids a cross-schema key and another service's table read, and the legacy key carries the ALS business date on the record, so the dictionary row and the missing column have to be resolved in favour of the target rules before the migration is written.

text: The profile accepts any rule ID that the registry holds for package ENTRY and asserts no literal value of its own; the fixtures and criteria carry the rule ID that the registry catalogue publishes for the admitting rule, and until it is published the tests name the rule ID only by reference to package ENTRY.
why: No source writes the identifier of the admitting rule of package ENTRY, and a test that asserts an invented identifier would pass while recording the wrong rule; the profile only needs the field to be present and held.
